10 supportive gifts after a difficult checkride or training setback

After a disappointing training day, a gift should offer support rather than a lesson about perseverance. The recipient may want to talk, take a break or make a practical plan later. This list starts with low-pressure gestures and leaves decisions about training to them.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Ask what would help and accept a small answer. Avoid jokes, motivational slogans or an unsolicited course intended to fix the result. Do not make public posts or share the story without permission. Practical help is most useful when it is specific and welcome.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    A meal they do not have to organize

    Choose familiar food and a comfortable setting. Offer company without requiring a detailed explanation of the day.

  2. 2

    A short supportive note

    Recognize the person and their effort without minimizing disappointment. Avoid predicting an outcome or setting a deadline for trying again.

  3. 3

    A quiet afternoon together

    Offer a walk, film or ordinary activity. Let the recipient decide whether aviation is part of the conversation.

  4. 4

    Help with an agreed practical task

    Taking care of a specific errand can create breathing room. Ask first rather than rearranging their plans uninvited.

  5. 5

    A favorite book or game

    Choose something enjoyable outside training. A distraction can be welcome without implying the person should abandon their goal.

  6. 6

    A small comfort package

    Use familiar snacks or simple everyday items. Keep it personal and avoid making the package a dramatic statement about the setback.

  7. 7

    A flexible contribution toward their next step

    Offer support only if the recipient wants it. They should decide how and when to use it.

  8. 8

    A photograph from a happy shared memory

    Choose a moment unrelated to performance or achievement. The point is connection rather than a comparison with better days.

  9. 9

    A future outing with no fixed date

    Give them something pleasant to look forward to. Keep the arrangement easy to postpone or decline.

  10. 10

    Your attention without advice

    Listen if they want to talk and respect it if they do not. A supportive conversation need not end with a solution.

These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read our selection approach and ATC disclosure.
